name: 0.4.0 — Moving boundary solver
body:
## Moving boundary solver support

Author and run VCell **moving-boundary** simulations directly from pyvcell.

- `vc.simulate_moving_boundary(biomodel, sim)` → `MovingBoundaryResult` (the moving front polygon plus per-element concentrations on the moving mesh, per output time).
- Authoring API: `Application.add_moving_boundary_sim(...)` (a `MovingB` simulation with `MovingBoundarySolverOptions`) and `Application.set_moving_boundary_front(velocity_x, velocity_y, ...)`.
- The VCML writer/reader round-trip the `MovingB` solver and its options.

### Install

```bash
pip install "pyvcell[mb]"
```

Pulls `pyvcell-mbsolver >= 1.0.3` and `libvcell >= 0.0.17` (both universal wheels, including Python 3.14).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

- **`cartesian_mesh_from_geometry`** — generate a VCell finite-volume `CartesianMesh` directly from a `Geometry`, without hand-building a biomodel:
  ```python
  import pyvcell.vcml as vc
  mesh = vc.cartesian_mesh_from_geometry(geometry, mesh_size=(64, 64, 64))
  mesh = geometry.to_cartesian_mesh()   # method form; defaults to image size, or resolution=50/axis
  ```
  Wraps the geometry in a minimal spatial biomodel, runs libvcell + the FV solver for one trivial step to produce the mesh, and returns the parsed `CartesianMesh`. Requires the `native` + `solver` extras; `Geometry.to_cartesian_mesh` delegates lazily so `pyvcell.vcml.models_geometry` stays import-light.
- Includes the output-function support from 0.3.2.

> Note: 0.3.2 was published separately for the output-function work; 0.3.3 supersedes it and adds the mesh-from-geometry feature.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/virtualcell/pyvcell/compare/0.3.2...0.3.3

name: Added Output Function Support
body: Exposed output annotated function capabilities

Typing & packaging follow-up to 0.3.0.

- **`py.typed`** — pyvcell now ships a [PEP 561](https://peps.python.org/pep-0561/) marker, so type checkers (mypy, pyright) use its inline annotations. The data models (e.g. `pyvcell.vcml.models_math.MathDescription`) are fully typed for downstream consumers.
- **Docs** — a new "Type checking" section covers the marker and the recommended consumer-side mypy override for projects that don't install every optional extra:
  ```toml
  [[tool.mypy.overrides]]
  module = ["pyvcell.*"]
  follow_imports = "silent"
  ```
  (Also corrected stale install docs: Python ≥3.12; the visualization stack is the `viz` extra.)

pyvcell's own type checking is unchanged (still `strict`).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/virtualcell/pyvcell/compare/0.3.0...0.3.1

## Highlights

- **MathDescription data model** — the generated math for each application (constants, functions, state variables, ODE/PDE/membrane jump conditions, and stochastic/particle constructs) is now parsed and exposed on `application.math_description` in the VCML reader/writer.
- **Lightweight install + optional extras** — the base `pip install pyvcell` is now slim (pydantic, lxml, numpy, numexpr). Heavy features live behind extras: `pip install "pyvcell[viz]"`, `[solver]`, `[remote]`, `[io]`, `[convert]`, `[native]`, or `[all]`. Imports are lazy (PEP 562), so the data models / VCML reader import without dragging in the solver/viz/remote/libvcell stack — and a missing extra raises a clear "install `pyvcell[...]`" error.
- **Lenient VCML reader** — best-effort physiology parse: unmodeled or malformed constructs are skipped instead of aborting the whole biomodel (preserving its `MathDescription` + `Geometry`). On a 2766-model public corpus, load success went from 77% → 100%.
- **Advection velocity on species mappings** — read/write `<Velocity>` on a `SpeciesMapping` (`velocity_x/_y/_z`). `Model.add_model_parameter(...)` now defaults `role="user defined"` to match VCell's Java representation.

## Other changes

- Data model refactored into focused modules: `models_base` / `models_geometry` / `models_math` / `models_app` / `models` (public API unchanged).
- Volume-variable shape robustness in the zarr writer (scalar / already-sized arrays, domain-optional names).
- `libvcell >= 0.0.15.3`.
- Headless test rendering — the test suite no longer opens blocking GUI windows.
- Maintenance: requires Python `>=3.12` (CI tests 3.12–3.14); removed the legacy poetry tooling.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/virtualcell/pyvcell/compare/0.2.4...0.3.0
